                    ### Question

A trans-esophageal echocardiogram demonstrates a thickened, calcified aortic valve with left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following heart sounds would likely be heard on auscultation of this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Diastolic rumble following an opening snap with an accentuated S1
opb. Early diastolic high-pitched blowing decrescendo murmur that is loudest at the left sternal border
opc. Crescendo-decrescendo murmur radiating to the carotids that is loudest at the right upper sternal border
opd. Holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla that is loudest at the apex
ope. Midsystolic click that is most prominent that is loudest at the apex

This is due to turbulent blood flow through the stenotic valve, leading to murmur generation. The presence of left ventricular hypertrophy and aortic valve calcification contribute to the generation of this specific heart sound.
